approved: Excise Tariff Amendment (Tobacco Duty Harmonisation) Bill 2017

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2017-08-10.72.1) to read the bill for a second time. In other words, they agreed with the main idea of the bill and can now discuss the bill in more detail. ### Main idea of the bill According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1718a/18bd007): > *The purposes of the [Excise Tariff Amendment (Tobacco Duty Harmonisation) Bill 2017](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r5893) (the Excise Bill) and the [Customs Tariff Amendment (Tobacco Duty Harmonisation) Bill 2017](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r5892) (the Customs Bill) (collectively, the Bills) are to amend the Excise Tariff Act 1921 and the Customs Tariff Act 1995 (the Acts) to increase the excise equivalent customs duty imposed on roll-your-own (RYO) tobacco and other products such as cigars, so as to more accurately standardise the taxation treatment between stick and other RYO tobacco.*

The bill increases excise on roll-your-own tobacco to match the cigarette rate, correcting a tax disparity by adjusting the per-kilogram duty over four years based on a new assumption of 0.7 grams of tobacco per cigarette.

Labor supported the tobacco duty harmonisation bills, which equalise excise on roll-your-own and cigarettes and are estimated to raise $360 million in excise and $35 million in GST over the forward estimates. The government adopted Labor’s previous tobacco excise plan, while roll-your-own use rose from 26% to 36% of smokers between 2007 and 2016.

The speaker supported the tobacco duty harmonisation bills raising cigarette prices by 12.5% annually for four years to $40 per pack, but warned this could turbocharge the illicit market, already costing $1.6 billion in lost revenue, and called for more law enforcement resources to monitor the prohibition-by-price effect.

The government will amend the Excise Tariff Act 1921 and Customs Tariff Act 1995 to harmonise duty on roll-your-own tobacco with cigarettes, adjusting the per-kilogram rate over four years from 1 September 2017 to better reflect the average 0.8-gram tobacco content assumed for manufactured cigarettes.
